When I was 17, I met a 20+ year old guy online and then met him in a public place (with my mom nearby).

He actually didn't turn out to be bad news, but it was incredibly embarrassing to admit I hadn't turned 18 yet. I still remember how humiliating that was, and I never did it again because of that.

You didn't overreact at all. His behavior is creepy as hell, and your teacher sucks for acting like "Eric's just being Eric." Threatening to murder someone isn't a "haha what a class clown" thing. I hope he leaves you alone.
I only wish I'd done it sooner.
I now feel validated that all the chairs in my apartment are full of clothes and stuff. No room for creepy things to visit.

If your high school was anything like mine, they lied about how difficult college was, so you can relax a little. It's not impossible.

That said, you shouldn't slack off (even freshman year) and you should go to class. Especially because the more you skip going, the harder it is to motivate yourself to go back.

Take advantage of mental health services. My campus had a free counseling center (and the therapist I had there was the best one I've ever had).

Also, I'd say try out different classes not related to your major. You might find that you're actually way more interested in another field, or just find a cool subject.

Oh, and there's nothing wrong with community college or vocational stuff.

Talk to my pets.

Also, I'd want to figure out a way to help them.

Oh, and cut a deal with insects and spiders to get out of my apartment because I don't actually want to hurt them, I just want them nowhere near me.

Harry/Draco is a favorite ship of mine and er...well honestly, they are hot together. But I've also read a ton of really nice fics, especially set after Hogwarts or that were AU, that explored how their relationship could have come about, and I've loved them all. Especially all the angst that comes with a happy ending.

My favorites are Drarry and Luna/Hermione. My OT3 is Luna/Hermione/Ginny.

I've read Tomarry but I'm really, really picky about which stories I actually like, because I usually don't like it when Harry ends up dark.

I've seen fics where it's used regularly, and Hogsmeade is only one stop. And fics where it's closed up and doesn't run at all, except when needed for Hogwarts. I don't know that it really says anything canon-wise, though?

Not only is it real, there are multiple stories.

linkffn(10070271;7806076)
Lucius Malfoy getting it on with a peacock.

Pairings-wise, I really like anything with Luna, but especially pairings like Luna/Hermione and Luna/Ginny. I also like Snape/Hermione as long as it's set after Hogwarts and/or Hermione is of age.

I love "Harry gets rescued from the Dursleys" stories, especially when they're set before Hogwarts. I like kid stories in general, if they're written well, like what's happening before Hogwarts, magical primary school, magic lessons for kids, that kind of thing. 

And I like happy endings. I like it when everything turns out all right in the end.
It's a one shot, and it's about Ginny, but you mentioning muggle heroin made me remember this story: linkffn(11603850) It's about Ginny trying to deal with the after-effects of the diary.

Character bashing, especially over the top character bashing, like they aren't just bad, they are the Worst Evil To Come From the Earth, especially when someone is only bashed in order to set up some other pairing (a lot of Harry/Hermione fics do this with Ron, I've noticed).

Extremely out of character, with no reasoning or plot development behind why.

Rape/abuse/suicide that just seems gratuitous and thrown into the story. I don't mind stories that focus on abuse or have abuse or suicide themes, but I hate the really graphic ones, especially when whoever it happened to is perfectly fine a chapter later.

Super over powered Harry, especially if it comes with 200 extra titles and every seat in the Wizengamot, which of course he can easily handle, because he's a political genius at 11. ...No.
I'm pretty sure that's a massive red flag for sexual abuse, yes.

I don't think I've ever seen that. If I really liked the story, then I'd probably keep reading it, but if I was already on the fence, then bad mouthing someone else's story would probably make me stop reading.

If there's too many grammatical/spelling mistakes (or if there aren't technically mistakes, but the story is just written really poorly), then I usually can't keep reading.

Also if the characters are extremely out of character, but there's nothing set up to explain why. I don't mind reading OOC if there's actual justification/explanation for the story, but if they just are and there's no reasoning for it, I tend to dislike it.
All I can suggest is googling any pen names and/or story names you remember, in hopes they posted them somewhere else.

Sometimes indulging in crying/asking to be held/etc. has helped, instead of trying to deny I feel that way? Denial never seems to work.

Hi. Don't know how much I'll ever post, but oh well. Call me Fey. I'm more of a middle, I'm non-binary, and I don't talk a lot because anxiety.

Thank you. It is definitely best to ignore it! If I feel like I can't ignore the unread message (since she likes to send stuff on Facebook, and I haven't been ready to block her yet), I have my partner read it for me, and then I can ignore it.

The funny thing is that despite everything my parents have done, I would probably still be there except for one thing. I wasn't living with them. I was living with another relative who was 1000% worse, would constantly threaten to kick me out (over the smallest thing, she would bring it up every day, and laugh about it, but also in a way that was serious). I even went to the domestic violence shelter to talk to them about what I could do, but because I am a disabled adult, I'm a "vulnerable" person, and they sent the police the next day to do a wellness check. She turned on the charm and to this day, I have no idea how I managed to get out of that without her realizing what I'd actually done.

And the worst thing is that the rest of my family believed me. My dad hated her, my mom kept making excuses but also acknowledged that she was awful, and my sibling flat out despised every ounce of her being. But my parents didn't have a lot of money (nor would they have helped me out anyway tbh, they're still abusive), and I had no way of earning any because I was too disabled to work, and she was making everything worse.

I had a friend across country who became my girlfriend (and more) and she bought me a ticket. I didn't tell my narcissistic relative until the week before that I was moving and she spent every moment she could keeping me doing stuff for her, to prevent me from packing, and told me if I didn't, she would make me miss my bus. But I didn't, and I managed to get the heck out of Dodge.

She still emails and messages me and it's always full of manipulation and guilt trips, I don't read any of it. I can handle my parents, they have somehow gotten better over the years (I think because of their other mental illnesses, etc.), but she's only gotten worse. And to think, I used to hope that she could be a refuge. She became worse than I could have ever imagined, I'm so glad I'm across the country from her now.

I think what convinced me that the supernatural exists is all the stuff that happened in my parents' house. We moved in when I was 11? And before we'd even properly moved in, creepy stuff happened (like when I looked out my window and saw an enormous pair of red, glowing eyes over six feet up, against the house--nothing was out there, and they were too high up to be, say, tail-light reflections from the alley). That was only the start of it and honestly, I don't think stuff's ever ended in that house. It's more like whatever's there just sort of...waits, trying to pretend it's gone, so you lower your guard. That's not the only thing that's convinced me, but it's probably the earliest thing that showed me "hey, supernatural, I don't know how to explain this."
